source.title: Investigating Sensitive Directions in GPT-2: An Improved Baseline and Comparative Analysis of SAEs

record.tranche_reason: The post uses SAE dictionary directions as candidate features in activation-perturbation analyses, but does not test superposition, capacity pressure, feature recovery, or feature dimensionality as described by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The post reports sensitivity results for SAE feature directions and reconstruction errors. These results measure output effects of perturbations, not whether the claim's proposed representational properties hold. The other versions are not tested.
record.test_reason: The post measures how much GPT2-small output changes when Layer 6 activations are perturbed along SAE feature directions, SAE error directions and random baselines. This functional-sensitivity measure does not test toy superposition (V1), capacity competition (V2), alternative causes of polysemanticity (V3), whether features are spread across neurons or recovered by SAEs (V4), the completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features (V5), or feature dimensionality (V6). The SAE-versus-cov-random comparison loosely relates to whether SAE directions are privileged, but it is a different construct. It is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct but incomplete. The authors also conclude three further points. Previous baselines were flawed because they subtracted the original activation. SAE errors are no longer pathologically large against the cov-random mixture baseline. Error extrapolation differs between traditional and end-to-end SAEs. They also find lower-L0 SAE features more impactful and e2e features no more impactful than traditional ones.
record.recipe_differences: The post uses activation perturbations to compare candidate SAE feature directions and baselines; it does not reproduce the toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with SAE type and L0; SAE reconstruction-error behavior also varies across layers. The post notes that the L0 pattern for end-to-end SAE errors depends on perturbation length and metric.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE reconstruction errors are not pathologically high-KL once compared with a cov-random mixture baseline at Layer 6, though this varies across layers (Figures 3-4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The apparent pathological sensitivity of SAE reconstruction errors is largely explained by an isotropic baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE feature directions' output impact relative to the cov-random baseline depends on SAE type and L0. Lower L0 gives larger impact, and e2e features have the least impact at matched L0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature directions are not uniformly privileged in output sensitivity; this depends on SAE training choices.

record.problems: The analysis primarily summarizes results with means, which the authors say may obscure the shape of individual perturbation curves. The relevant SAE feature results are described qualitatively here without numerical values or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported perturbation comparisons, including SAE reconstruction-error and baseline comparisons, are omitted because they do not measure any of the claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy networks, sparsity transition or geometry.
No capacity competition or polysemanticity measurement.
No measure of feature spread across neurons or of SAE recovery of sparse features.
No test of SAE feature completeness, stability across runs, or canonicity; only output sensitivity to single directions.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r1-r3 are correctly linked to 'none'. The reconstruction-error and baseline results are omitted from the rows, as rows_left_out declares. That is acceptable since they bear on no version. The post motivates sensitive directions by computation-in-superposition toy models, but it does not test superposition.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network superposition, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry is tested.
No capacity competition, dedicated dimensions, or polysemanticity is tested.
No alternative causes of polysemanticity are tested.
The post does not test whether model features are spread across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features.
SAE feature completeness, stability, and canonicity are not tested.
The post does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.value: All SAE features have a greater impact on model output than isotropic random directions; compared with cov-random mixture, the effect varies by SAE type and L0.
rows.note: Qualitative result stated in the text; no numerical values are given.
